question: What color and dimensional limits apply to crosswalk markings, including transverse crosswalk lines?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Crosswalk markings must be white, and transverse lines, when used, must be between 6 inches and 24 inches wide. The marked crosswalk itself must be at least 6 feet wide, increasing to a minimum of 8 feet at non-intersection crosswalks where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater. The same 6-to-24-inch limit applies to the transverse lines that establish the limits of a ladder crosswalk. Standards (mandatory): - "The transverse lines used to establish the limits of the ladder crosswalk shall not be less than 6 inches or greater than 24 inches in width." - As shown in the page evidence for Section 3C.03: "Crosswalk markings shall be white. When used, transverse lines shall not be less than 6 inches or greater than 24 inches in width." [Image 2] - Also shown in Section 3C.03: "Except as provided in Paragraph 6 of this Section, the minimum width of a marked crosswalk shall be 6 feet," and "At a non-intersection crosswalk where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater, the minimum width of the crosswalk shall be 8 feet." [Image 2] Guidance (recommended): - Transverse line crosswalk markings should be limited to locations controlled by traffic control signals or on approaches controlled by STOP or YIELD signs. - To provide contrast with aesthetic surface treatments, a gap of at least one-half the width of the white transverse line used to establish the crosswalk, but not less than 6 inches, should be used between the white crosswalk lines and the aesthetic surface treatment, such as unmarked pavement or a black contrast line. Options (permitted): - High-visibility crosswalk markings may be used where additional conspicuity is desired for a crosswalk over transverse line crosswalk markings. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3C-1 depicts the dimensional limits for each crosswalk design: transverse lines 6–24 inches wide with a 6 ft minimum crosswalk width; longitudinal bars 12–60 inches long (not to exceed 2.5 times the bar width) and 12–24 inches wide; ladder designs combining both; and bar pairs of 8–12-inch bars, all with a footnote that the minimum crosswalk width shall be 8 feet where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater at a non-intersection crosswalk. - [Image 2] Page 631 shows Section 3C.03 (Design of Crosswalk Markings), including the Standard that crosswalk markings shall be white, transverse lines shall be 6–24 inches wide, and the 6-foot (or 8-foot) minimum crosswalk widths, together with Figure 3C-1. - [Image 3] Page 632 shows Sections 3C.04 (Transverse Line Crosswalks) and 3C.05 (High-Visibility Crosswalks), including the guidance limiting transverse line crosswalks to signal- or STOP/YIELD-controlled locations. - [Image 4] Page 17 is a table of contents listing Chapter 3C Crosswalk Markings sections, confirming section locations but adding no dimensional requirements. - [Image 5] Page 664 shows Section 3H.03/3H.04 material and Figure 3H-1, including the guidance on a contrast gap of at least half the transverse line width (not less than 6 inches) between crosswalk lines and aesthetic surface treatments. Citations: - Section 3C.07 Standard §4 (p.592) - Section 3C.04 Guidance §1 (p.591) - Section 3H.03 Guidance §11 (p.623) - Section 3C.05 Option §1 (p.591) - Section 3C.01 Support §1 (p.589) - Section 3C.01 Support §2 (p.589) - Figure 3C-1 (p.590) - Page 631 - Page 632 - Page 664
gold_answer: Crosswalk markings must be white. Where transverse lines are used, each line must be at least 6 inches and no more than 24 inches wide. Except for certain ramp-terminal cases, the marked crosswalk should be at least 6 feet wide.
